content.v: 近日国产游戏《 昭和米国物语 》制作人罗翔宇接受外媒AUTOMATON采访，他确认游戏全部内容已开发完成，现阶段团队重心转向打磨优化战斗手感等细节。本作将于2026年发售，登陆PC和PS5平台，发售前不会推出试玩版。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793570368_555663_jpg_r.jpg
《昭和米国物语》游戏跳过全部过场动画的纯主线时长约25小时。完整观看全部剧情演出，流程时长几乎翻倍，支线、收集内容游玩时长因人而异。本作没有使用传统简单‑普通‑困难命名，三档难度分别叫令和巨婴、平成废宅、昭和男儿。
昭和男儿(高难度)：战斗惩罚强化，残血受伤大幅提高，适合硬核挑战向玩家。
平成废宅(标准难度)：制作人最推荐，挑战适中，不容易卡关，可以完整体验战斗系统设计。
令和巨婴(最低难度)：自带自动连招，制作人戏称 “连猫都能通关”，适合只想看剧情、习惯长按普攻的玩家。
高难度通关只会给到额外道具，不会锁成就/奖杯，全部奖杯任意难度均可解锁。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793570368_282864_jpg_r.jpg
采访中还谈及本地化立场，罗翔宇表示不会为海外玩家删减、修改源自国内网络环境的本土文化梗，海外玩家看不懂也属于文化交流的一部分。开发组也知悉线下试玩反馈的战斗手感问题，会在正式版继续打磨优化，但暂未公布确切发售日。

content.v: BLACKPINK成员Lisa近日在美国主持人Jake Shane的播客节目《Therapuss》中分享了一段昔日暧昧经历。她曾邀请暧昧对象为同桌的母亲、好友及自己支付寿司餐费，但对方当场拒绝，最终仍由她结账。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793569467_423596_jpg_r.jpg
Lisa表示，当时她与母亲和好友来到自己喜欢的寿司店，席间半开玩笑地询问对方是否愿意替一行人买单，对方随即回答“不要”。她起初以为这同样是一句玩笑，还期待对方可能私下结账制造惊喜，但直至用餐结束也没有等到。
她强调，自己并非每次约会都要求男方付钱，也有能力承担餐费。令她在意的是母亲和好友当时也在场。在她看来，对方若愿意主动请客，能够体现重视和付出的心意。Jake Shane则认为，如果男方正在追求她，这样做或许可以展现更多诚意。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793569597_848532.jpg
这段分享引发了不同意见。有人认为，追求阶段与长辈一同用餐时，主动请客会显得更体贴；也有人认为，对方没有替Lisa及其亲友支付餐费的义务，争议反映出双方对约会和金钱往来的期待并不一致。

https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793566168_718073_jpg_r.jpg
新版异形会继续追踪并适应玩家行为，同时拥有更多反应方式，更快识别玩家习惯，行动也将更加主动。玩家若反复使用同一种误导手段，未必每次都能奏效。开发者还表示，同一问题将有多种解决方式，希望不同玩家经历的流程有所区别。
本作舞台将从封闭空间站扩展到Kurosaki星球，场景包括开放荒野和小型聚落。异形可以利用环境与动态天气展开追猎：雷声可能掩盖它的移动声，暴雨和黑暗能够隐藏踪迹，恶劣环境还可能导致玩家依赖的设备发生故障。室内外场景的转换则用于制造暴露感与安全感的起伏。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261030/1793343775_620876_jpg_r.jpg

others.title: 编年史：中世纪开发商在发布之前“面临真正的关闭风险”，因为资金“不再到位”

content.v: 《编年史： 中世纪 》开发商Raw Power Games宣布，维持工作室和项目所需的资金已经中断。缺少这笔资金后，团队无法继续制作游戏，工作室目前面临关闭风险。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793566116_265773_jpg_r.jpg
《编年史：中世纪》是一款主打动态中世纪世界和大规模战斗的开放世界沙盒游戏，开发时间已经超过四年。游戏原计划于2027年初在Steam开启抢先体验。
此次资金问题出现得较为突然。团队在10月仍持续发布开发日志，其中还详细介绍了中世纪纹章及其在游戏中的呈现方式，此前公开信息并未显露工作室已经陷入危机。Raw Power Games表示，项目已经非常接近可以推出的阶段，抢先体验版本“触手可及”，团队构建多年的世界也开始展现完整面貌。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260914/1789338038_449836_jpg_r.jpg
工作室表示不会放弃争取生存，并呼吁关注者继续将游戏保留在愿望单中、持续讨论项目。目前，团队尚未公布现有资金还能维持多久，也未确认新的投资者或融资安排。工作室关闭及游戏取消仍是现实风险，但尚未成为既定结果；原定抢先体验计划能否实现，将取决于团队能否及时获得替代资金。

content.v: 近日外媒ComicBook作者呼吁任天堂将《 塞尔达传说：风之杖HD 》和《塞尔达传说：黄昏公主HD》移植到Switch或Switch 2。该主张以《塞尔达传说：时之笛》重制版为切入点，并非任天堂公布的移植计划。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793566053_183802_jpg_r.jpg
《塞尔达传说：风之杖HD》和《塞尔达传说：黄昏公主HD》分别于2013年和2016年登陆Wii U，至今没有Nintendo Switch或Nintendo Switch 2版本。前者通过高分辨率画面和玩法调整改进GameCube原作，后者也加入了视觉强化及其他优化。作者因此认为，两款HD版仍是体验相应作品的重要版本。
作者主张，在《塞尔达传说：时之笛》重制版获得独立宣传空间后，任天堂也应把现有的Wii U版本带到当前平台。即使只是直接移植，也能让缺少旧硬件的新玩家接触这些作品，并方便老玩家重新体验。
若为新版本加入性能提升、控制优化和现代硬件兼容性，作者认为两款作品会更适合Switch 2。《塞尔达传说：风之杖》和《塞尔达传说：黄昏公主》在美术风格、氛围及冒险结构上各有特色。目前，任天堂尚未公布相关移植计划。

content.v: 近日一名爱好者展示了《 上古卷轴5：天际 》虚幻5渲染改造项目，并用安装超过1500个模组的版本测试兼容性。该项目没有将整款游戏迁移至虚幻5，目前仍是早期技术展示。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793565904_727227_jpg_r.jpg
这套方案保留Bethesda原有的Creation Engine，用其处理游戏逻辑、用户界面、非玩家角色行为和脚本；虚幻引擎5则负责几何绘制、阴影与全局光照，其中Lumen和Nanite分别参与光照及几何处理。项目还计划原生整合DLSS和帧生成。
作者表示，维持现有模组生态是项目的重要目标。测试版本安装了Requiem、Frostfall和SunHelm等模组，演示中的MCM菜单、对话与任务仍可运行，原因是这类模组的系统脚本通常不会直接介入渲染。
按照作者的说法，纹理包、三维模型和光照模组也可兼容。不过，ENB、Community Shaders等直接修改原有渲染管线的第三方DLL预计无法继续使用。
现阶段的演示仍有多项问题，包括加载画面不同步、植被和岩石短暂显示为缺失纹理时的粉色、水体透明异常及阴影闪烁。角色进入溪木镇后，性能也出现明显下降。作者计划先修复着色器并稳定帧率，之后再考虑公开发布。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 英国百万富翁、社交媒体创作者马克·蒂尔伯里近日发布视频，从娱乐成本角度讨论购买《GTA6》是否“省钱”。他按照一系列假设推算，玩家留在家中玩游戏，理论上可以避免5000美元的外出开销，这段视频随后引发传播。

蒂尔伯里在英国一家商店拿起游戏展示盒，并用计算器算了一笔账：假设游戏售价为99.99美元、完成流程需要80小时，每小时娱乐成本约为1.24美元；若再计入支线任务和大型开放地图，成本甚至可能降至每小时约0.5美元。
他进一步假设，玩家每晚游玩4小时并持续50个晚上。如果这些晚上原本都会外出，每晚在饮食、酒水和活动上花费约100美元，总开销便会达到5000美元。因此，宅家玩游戏理论上可以免去这笔支出。
注意，这套算法建立在特定售价、游玩时长及消费习惯之上，只是蒂尔伯里的个人说法，并非普遍适用的理财结论。

content.v: 《守望先锋》未来仍有可能重新推出可玩的PvE叙事任务，但这不代表完整剧情战役已经重启。游戏总监Aaron Keller表示，团队不会彻底排除PvE内容回归，不过重新制作完整战役将是规模截然不同的工程。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261016/1792101694_666586_jpg_r.jpg
Keller回顾称，此前上线的PvE活动推出时吸引了大量关注，也帮助游戏推进了世界观故事，但玩家参与度没有达到团队预期，热度随后迅速下降。这类任务需要投入可观的开发资源，相比之下，电影短片等叙事形式能够以更少的开发消耗讲述故事。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261102/1793565653_117977_jpg_r.jpg
如果PvE内容回归，规模较小、对主要竞技玩法影响有限的体验更有可能出现。不过，Keller使用的是“不会排除”这一表述，并未确认任何具体项目已经立项。
《守望先锋》最初曾规划深度合作战役，设想让玩家在故事模式中升级和改造英雄，并以更系统的方式推进世界观。该战役后来取消，之后由更短、更简单且更新不频繁的PvE任务承接，相关任务最终也停止推出。
Keller认为，若现在重新制作一套接近最初构想的完整战役，其规模可能需要另设一支团队，并将其当作“一款全新的游戏”开发。小型PvE任务仍留有回归空间，但原规划式完整战役现阶段不能视为已经重启。

content.v: Polymarket预测市场对《GTA6》Metacritic媒体均分给出了当前定价：游戏最终达到90分或以上的概率为96%，但达到98分或以上的概率仅为22%。市场参与者普遍预期本作能进入90分以上区间，对其冲击97至98分则更加谨慎。

items.title: Jagex 与一款受 RuneScape 启发的闲置游戏合作，将续集变成了官方衍生作品
items.summary: Melvor Idle 2 has gained a subtitle: A RuneScape Adventure.

content.v: It's easy to knock old-school RPGs, especially grindfests like RuneScape, for being games where you endlessly and sometimes mindlessly make numbers go up. But Melvor Idle, which self-bills as a RuneScape-inspired idle adventure game that claims to squeeze the genre into its "purest form," leans into that—and Jagex has partnered with developer Games by Malcs to make the RuneScape connection official.

The announcement blog from Jagex reads, "Melvor Idle takes a lot of inspiration from RuneScape and you can just feel it," adding that Jagex's support (and branding) is intended to help make the game "even bigger … while Melvor Idle 2 doesn’t take place in Gielinor, we think a fan-built idle game inspired by our MMOs is more than worthy of the title."

This isn't the first time Jagex has collaborated with Games by Malcs. It became the first Melvor Idle's publisher five years ago, albeit without a branding tweak. While RuneScape has had its fair share of monetization controversies over the years (you can see just how skeptical people were of the partnership when it was first announced on Reddit ), it doesn't seem like Melvor has been compromised by trouble along those lines—the announcement blog proudly proclaims the sequel will have "no microtransactions."

Beyond that, it seems like a bigger version of the familiar idle RPG with overhauled visuals and a higher level cap of 120. You might find it a bit odd that it's a "RuneScape Adventure" that doesn't take place in the MMO's setting, but I'm not sure how many people are really invested in Jagex's games for the scintillating lore and worldbuilding. If you end up feeling like a stranger in a strange land, you can always hire someone to spam "buying gf" in a chat window while you get your idle on.

items.title: 《侠盗猎车手 6》预告了一些即将推出的广播电台，其音乐策划一如既往地强大
items.summary: I can already picture my late-night Leonida drives to these bangers.

content.v: Grand Theft Auto's radio stations have long stood as an integral part of the series' whole vibe—either offering time capsules of the times each game was set in (Vice City), or offering a realistic blend of classic and modernity a la Grand Theft Auto 5's excellent music curation.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/WcCZiWMVteuU25phgoBuD8-1920-80.png
Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.

I've been just a tad giddy to discover what awaits me in Grand Theft Auto 6's car stereos when the game launches on November 19, which has me surprised that Rockstar teasing six of its upcoming stations earlier this month completely flew under my radar.

Well, now I've had a gander and listened to all 12 minutes of its DJs bantering and a peppering of bangers between. And I gotta say, I'm already jazzed to speed down Leonida's highways with some of these stations at full volume.

Rockstar's licensed music curation rarely misses, and that very much seems to be the continuing trend with Grand Theft Auto 6. While we don't know just how many radio stations there are in total yet—this is the first game where we'll be able to tune in to both terrestrial music stations and podcasts, it being 2026 and all—but the six that were teased were the exact kind of flavours I've come to expect from the series.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jdFL3AW5u4Tcz2PYphDGfZ-1920-80.jpg

There's Latin station Cocoteo FM, classic country Back Country Radio, African channel AfroBANK FM, all-out metal hub The Chamber 106.6, pop banger central Flash FM, and hip-hop destination Dirty South Classics. I'm already 100% here for The Chamber's setlist, being an elder emo and all, with bands like Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer making their way onto Leonida's airwaves. But I'm also jazzed to see newer blood on the scene, like Bad Bunny's appearance on Cocoteo.

My biggest interest was in Flash FM, though. Non-Stop Pop has become such an iconic radio station for me, thanks to some excellent song choices and Cara Delevigne's delightfully deadpan delivery. It doesn't seem like I'm going to be disappointed, though—Alex Consani takes up the mantle as model-turned-radio-host alongside the excellent artist Robyn (of Bulletproof fame), and hearing one of my favourite songs in MGMT's Electric Feel is all the confidence I need in Rockstar's keen ear.

While the previews do show criminally little interactions between the hosts (it seems like Grand Theft Auto 6 is going for duos across all its stations, presumably for some easy back-and-forth banter), I'm sure there'll still be satire in droves to come.

items.title: GOG希望恢复实体游戏，但这是“一件非常非常复杂的事情”
items.summary: "You click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. Th

content.v: I remember when I'd get bored as a kid, I'd marvel at the back covers of my older brother's PC game boxes—stuff like Guild Wars: Factions and the original World of Warcraft box, the inner cover of which showed a dwarf thwacking a yeti with that one epic sword that looked like a lightsaber. Even back then, the long switch to digital was underway, seemingly for good. But what if we could go back to the glory days of big, embossed boxes and girthy manuals?

That's the "dream" of GOG's senior business development and partnerships manager, Marcin Paczynski, as he recently told Gamesradar . Specifically, he wants to see a world where you "would be able to buy physical versions of [games] on GOG … You go to your shelf on GOG, you click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. That would be a perfect scenario."

I'm sure most PC gaming diehards would agree that, yes, an option to buy physical games—especially older games in a precarious state with regard to preservation—would be pretty neat. Even if you're the sort to snag DRM-free copies of everything you own, a disc makes a game easier to show off, keep close in the event that your hard drive explodes, or place in the seat across from you at a Michelin star restaurant.

The problem for GOG is that physical distribution is basically an entirely different business to running a digital storefront. "Because we are talking about physical media, we need to think about logistics, we need to think about storage," Paczynski said, adding that it's "a very, very complicated thing." But the idea has been on the company's collective mind "for years now," so he's not ruling it out.

If you don't want to wait, there's always projects like Big Box Collection that let you print your own facsimiles. Or buy used! A few scratches and a giant sticker reading "PROPERTY OF TREVOR" just lends character, right?

items.title: Valve 失传已久的《传送门》前传原型在近 20 年后再次上线
items.summary: F-Stop was a result of a post-Orange Box, 2007 Valve game jam.

content.v: As reported by Kotaku , a near-mythical canceled Valve game called F-Stop has been reconstructed from material contained in separate leaks. Direct access to the build seems a little shaky at the moment, but full playthroughs of the game, like this one by Meme Man? on YouTube , are starting to pop up online.

Most of F-Stop's assets came out in this August's Steam "teraleak," but the final pieces⁠—F-Stop's source code and mapsrc data⁠—were only just acquired by the Valve Cut Content Team Discord, which appears to have gone private amid all the newfound attention over F-Stop. With the Discord currently invite-only, you gotta know a guy (or know a guy who knows a guy) to play it yourself.

The Half-Life Wiki has the skinny on F-Stop's origins in the "Directed Design Experiments." Following the megahit launch of the Orange Box in 2007, Gabe Newell effectively shut Valve down for a three-month game jam that produced five prototypes, F-Stop among them.

It applied Team Fortress 2's cel-shaded art style to a vision of Aperture Science in its prime, all mid-century wood-paneled office optimism. F-Stop's central mechanic was a camera that could capture objects in the world, then place them elsewhere to solve puzzles. The excellent 2023 game Viewfinder would apply a similar concept to a full commercial release.

But while loved internally at Valve, F-Stop's playtests were apparently more tepid. The game was shelved, though elements of its worldbuilding would appear in Portal 2 and Aperture Desk Job. It's fun to recognize some of these early ideas in the F-Stop longplays: From the jump, we get a version of Cave Johnson (sadly sans-J.K. Simmons in prototype) talking to the player, as well as the first instance of Aperture Personality Cores as companions in the puzzling.

Given F-Stop's "road not taken" nature, particularly compared to the megathit Left 4 Dead and Portal 2 that would follow, I don't really mourn the fact that we never got to play its final version. It is, however, extremely cool that the prototype game is now preserved for posterity.

items.title: 作曲家兼设计师 Lena Raine 解释了 Pigstep 如何改变 Minecraft 的音乐风格：“我不断听到的提示是‘哦，Pigstep 太棒了，他们想要更多棒子’”
items.summary: The composer for Celeste and Minecraft guides us through the games on her PC.

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/DEwkbfkEmfdtjT5P9ybme-1920-80.png

Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Lena Raine's formative gaming experience was playing Myst on a Mac Quadra 610, exploring Cyan Worlds' enigmatic island in parallel with her father: "We each had our own playthrough, so we were sending each other notes in the little journal that it came with," she says. "I still have the little book that we wrote in."

Raine always aspired to be a composer for video games, but she initially joined the industry as a games tester for Nintendo America, working several other testing jobs before being hired by ArenaNet as a game designer. While working on Guild Wars 2 , Raine designed a bell-choir minigame for the MMO's Winter's Day Christmas update, including writing the music for it. "It was a bizarre first-step into game music," she says. "But that eventually led to at last some visibility for the other music I was writing."

After leaving ArenaNet, Raine wrote the soundtrack for 2018's Celeste , and spent several years composing music for Minecraft , including several of its most popular 'Disc' tracks like Pigstep , Creator , and Otherside . Raine is currently writing music for the early access volleyball RPG Beastieball , while also returning to game design with her own project ANOTHEREAL , an RPG with schmup-style combat. "I have been working on [it] basically since the pandemic," she says. "I'm trying to aim to have something released within the decade."

Raine took a break from her various projects to show me around the digital concert hall of her steam library. We discussed Deadlock , sorted her schmup collection, and took a trip down MMO memory lane.
What game are you currently playing?
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/hyJZqKLd6d2piRXx9NEXq9-1920-80.jpg

The current game that I'm playing is Deadlock. I've been playing it for a while now, basically since it was pretty early in that beta, alpha, whatever phase. I play with my wife and some other friends that we've got.

I've been having a lot of fun with it. I've never been a MOBA person and I've never been a competitive shooter person either. Usually, I get tremendously frustrated with online competitive shooters because I'm not very good. I'm not great at those sorts of games.

But I love the style and the world that Valve has made for Deadlock. I love spooky occult stuff. I just love that entire vibe. A lot of my personal online characters are like demon girl aesthetics, and so I'm just like "This is a game for me".

I've been really committed to learning at least one character, so I've been focusing on Ivy, which is the gargoyle. She's awesome. She's from the first set of characters. I initially just laser-focussed on her. I was just like "Oh, she's really cool".
What was the previous game you played, and is it still installed
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/hCYfaQA8CMHBrQRd4WBEWR-1920-80.jpg

The Mermaid Mask . I was playing it on the Steam Machine, so technically it's still installed. But it's a single-player, linear story game, so I will probably uninstall it at some point to save space.

It's still installed because I finished it yesterday, or two days ago. But I really loved that game. I played the previous game— Tangle Tower —in the Detective Grimoire series, and they just have such a playful way of designing characters and presenting them. The voice acting is really good. The mysteries are fun and interesting to figure out as you're playing through it. It's a detective point-and-click adventure, gathering clues and talking to all the suspects.

There's just [a] ridiculous amount of items in the game that you can ask everyone about. And it's all just voice dialogue about all of them. I'm just such a completionist about it. I just sit in front of the TV and I've been listening to the characters talk about 30 different items for an hour.
What is the oldest game (by release date) currently installed on your PC?
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eekJsfxur2n2zuc58XJnke-1920-80.jpg

The one that I really wanted to talk about is Final Fantasy 11 , which is one of the first PC games that I got fully obsessed with when I was younger, at high school into college basically. It's got uninstalled and reinstalled over the years. But I have it installed. I've checked in on my character, who has been there since the initial release date … I played a little Tarutaru character and mostly was a red mage and monk.

The interesting piece of history with me and Final Fantasy 11 is that I initially imported it from Japan. It has since transferred over to English servers primarily. But when I initially started playing the game, it was not out in the US yet, and you had to import the game. You had to make a Japanese account with a Japanese address. But there were forums set up for people that wanted to import the game.

So I joined these forums, and these were people who also played like Phantasy Star Online on the Dreamcast, so we were all buzzing about this new game Final Fantasy 11. So there were instructions of like "here's translated screenshots of every single setup thing to do."

I had taken one year of Japanese in high school. So I knew enough to navigate a menu. I didn't know how to converse very well in Japanese, but I knew what the characters for like black mage, red mage, warrior, attack, level up, those sorts of things.

[But] the thing about Final Fantasy 11 is it was such a deeply social game, because to level up past a certain point you needed to join a party. You could not solo past a certain point. So people would group in in levelling parties, and unless I was playing with friends, I would be in a group of Japanese players that I was trying to communicate with, and it really depended on the sophistication of the conversation that was going on that I could blend in or out myself as speaking English.

The majority of friendships that I had was with the English-speaking community, and it's funny because a number of those people have gone on to have some pretty illustrious careers. One of the people that I played with was Maximilian Dood, who's a fairly well-to-do YouTuber now. Another friend that I played PSO and Final Fantasy with was Jason Oestreicher who worked for Giant Bomb for a while. So I have these weird industry connections from playing this import Final Fantasy game years ago.
What is the highest number of hours you have in any given game, according to Steam?
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Lm65SSadSsNLi7wj8DWW2e-1920-80.jpg

The highest number of hours is Elden Ring at 282 hours. However, not on Steam, I looked this up also, Final Fantasy 14 , I logged into my character and did the playtime conversion, and it's 1,308 hours.

I feel like I've talked a lot about Final Fantasy, [so] to talk a little bit about Elden Ring. I've played pretty much all of the Dark Souls games and mostly attempted to do co-op with them because my wife and I love to play the games together, and we always have a very rough experience when it comes to FromSoft online stuff, because it's very insistent on opening yourself up to adversity when you're playing together with friends.

But with Elden Ring, when that came out, this was right before we moved to Canada … [when] we were in this transit dead space where all our stuff is half-packed and we just need to find the right place. And so we were just calming our brains down by playing Elden Ring together.

items.title: “绝对的庞然大物”：雄心勃勃的 FPS Selaco 正在进行大规模更新，其尺寸增加了一倍，并添加了“可以发射真正爆炸的重机枪”
items.summary: Selaco: The Machines of War arrives later this month.

content.v: If you're a fan of first-person shooters and haven't played Selaco , you should. Built in the Doom engine and inspired by FEAR , Half-Life and System Shock , Selaco is a rollicking, dizzyingly ambitious sci-fi FPS where you battle a mercenary incursion of a vast, city-sized space station that's home to the last of humanity.

Launched into Steam early access in 2024, Selaco's first chapter alone is as long as some entire '90s shooters. Now, developer Altered Orbit Studios is preparing to release an update that will not only double the length of the game, but also introduce a wide array of new features and rework much of its existing design.

Described by Altered Orbit as "an absolute behemoth", Selaco: The Machines of War introduces the second of a planned three chapters to the FPS. Chapter two comprises 19 new campaign maps, which apparently amounts to "6-8 hours of additional content". Alongside further story elements and a voice for the protagonist, the chapter also introduces what sounds like a persistent enemy, in the form of "an unstoppable machine" that is "hunting you down."

Naturally, this second chapter also adds new weapons and enemies, with the former including a minigun and "a heavy machine gun that fires literal explosions". I don't know how that would work, but I'm keen to find out! Alongside your equipped arsenal, players will be able to use new deployable weapons like mini-turrets and sentinel drones, while the update also introduces a "heavy ordnance system" that lets you wield large, disposable weapons scattered across the battlefield, Gears of War -style.

As well as completely new stuff, Altered Orbit says the update will also enhance a lot of existing content. The FEAR inspired enemy AI, for example, has been "rewritten almost entirely from scratch" to facilitate smarter tactics and better decision making. The rewrite also introduces a new "rally" system and NPC area patrolling when not in combat—an addition designed to give players more agency in when and how fighting begins. Oh, and the entire first chapter has been given an overhaul that introduces "improved set pieces" and "new surprises".

And those are just the headline changes. Other improvements mentioned by Altered Orbit include a new lighting system, an overhauled particle system to make combat even more spectacular, improved navigation through Selaco's massive, mazey levels, new voice lines to make enemy communication even more lifelike, better controls, new music, and more. It almost sounds too good to be true, but I've played Chapter 1 and I know Altered Orbit can cook with rocket fuel, so none of this is beyond the studio's capability.

Selaco: The Machines of War arrives on November 13. The scale of the changes means that old saves will no longer be compatible. But if you don't fancy replaying the reworked first episode, you will be able to jump in at the outset of Chapter 2.

content.v: Chronicles: Medieval is an impressive looking open-world sandbox where players explore a dynamic Medieval world and fight in massive, authentic battles. It's been in development for more than four years and is due to launch into Steam early access early in 2027.
However, there is a very real chance this will no longer happen, as developer Raw Power Games suddenly faces closure after funding for its game was pulled.

On Friday, Raw Power Games posted a statement to Steam and on social media channels (via IGN ), explaining how the studio has suddenly found itself in dire straits. "Due to circumstances outside our control, the necessary funding for Raw Power Games is no longer in place," the studio wrote. "Without it, we can't keep building Chronicles: Medieval, and right now the studio is at real risk of closing."

This appears to be a sudden development. Through October, the studio had been posting regular development updates, including an incredibly detailed deep dive on Medieval coats of arms and how they would appear in the game. None of it suggested a studio that's in trouble, so it seems this has caught Raw Power off guard.

By the sounds of it, Chronicles: Medieval isn't all that far away from being done, either. Or at least ready for its planned alpha launch: "What makes it hurt is how close we are. Early access is within reach," Raw Power Games writes in its statement. "The world we've been building for years is finally starting to feel alive, and we have so much we've been thrilled to show you."

Chronicles: Medieval first appeared on our radar last year , not without some controversy. At the time, Raw Power Games was super excited about using generative AI for its games. Not only was the studio using Midjourney to generate (terrible) concept art, but company COO Jakob Rasmussen told Danish newspaper Ingeniøren that genAI was "at the core of our vision", adding that "When the technology is ready—and perhaps a little sooner—we'll be willing to stick our necks out and put it into the game."

Yet the company quickly changed its tune on this point, with CTO Caspar Strandbygaard telling PC Gamer that Chronicles: Medieval was "100% handcrafted with no use of generative AI." Strandbygaard admitted that Raw Power was still "curious" about the technology, but regarding Chronicles specifically, he stressed that "every asset in the game is built by our extremely talented team of passionate developers. It is not generated by AI."

While the situation seems grim for Raw Power, the studio says that it is "not going down without a fight" and has urged fans of the game to "keep Chronicles: Medieval on your wishlist and keep talking about it." How much road Raw Power has remaining before it's forced to close isn't clear. But since the game is allegedly close to being in a releasable state, it may be able to secure new funding relatively soon.

items.title: 不仅仅是 Steam：过去两个月，Itch.io 上每天创建的新游戏页面翻了一番，人工智能可能是罪魁祸首
items.summary: "The number of downloads and purchases has *not* doubled."

content.v: It seems it isn't just Steam that's being flooded with AI slop. Indie games storefront itch.io has reported that the number of new game pages being created per day on the site has doubled in the past two months, and just like Valve's much bigger distribution service, the finger is being pointed at AI.

Over on Bluesky, itch.io shared an image of a bar chart labelled "game events". The chart shows that, between August 3 and October 30, the number of new game pages being created per day has risen from around 3,000 to regularly surpassing 6,000. It's a ratio that more or less matches the increase in Steam demos showcased at the most recent Next Fest , which rose from around 4,000 to over 8,000.

While Itch doesn't explicitly point the finger at AI as the cause, it heavily infers it. When Bluesky user Tommy's Homemade Games asked "Do you know why?" Itch responded "take a guess" followed by emojis of a crying face and a robot. Another Bluesky account, BardZaku, asked "is it AI dreck?" to which the account replied with an emoji of a face with bags under its eyes.

The rapid uptick in Itch pages also coincides with the launch of Claude Opus 5, which arrived on July 24. The latest iteration of Anthropic's LLM—which is now at version 5.5—has proved particularly adept at reverse engineering code. This has had a bunch of knock-on effects in various areas of game development, ranging from much faster decompilations of old games, to Steam being flooded with AI slop, and developers cancelling public demos out of concerns their games will be cloned.

Anthropic has since updated Claude to reign in its ability to directly copy games, but it's currently hard to tell whether it has stemmed the broader flow of AI generated games. Indeed, it's worth pointing out that AI Generated games now comprise a good portion of the pages listed on Itch. Out of 1,769,316 listed on Itch at the time of writing, 131,929 are tagged as AI Generated, approximately 7.5% of the total. That's a lot, considering how long AI coding tools have been around.

But to play devil's advocate, Itch is a storefront that allows AI games, and if people are downloading and enjoying these games, then adding them to the store is fair enough, right? Well , Itch also points out that, although the number of games appearing on Itch per day has doubled, "the number of downloads and purchases has *not* doubled". This suggests these AI games are clogging up the site for nobody's benefit, not even the people 'making' them.

The question, then, is what's to be done about all this? The replies to Itch's initial post are filled with calls to ban AI generated games from the store. But as pointed out by AI researcher Mike Cook, simply banning these games is unlikely to solve the problem.

"I think that would be a good move. But it won't change this graph, unfortunately," Cook wrote on Bluesky. "You need a team of people to enforce it, or a very dicey public reporting system. Even then, it's a lot harder to detect than people think." Valve has also cast doubt on the efficacy of a ban on AI coding tools for games released on Steam, though its opinion is heavily influenced by the company's laissez-faire approach to operating its storefront.

Another possibility is to simply let this trend play out. There is a viral element to the ongoing surge in AI generated games, as people post their vibe-coded works online for attention and social media clout. But Itch's statement suggests that people aren't properly engaging with most of the games being uploaded.

Hence, it's possible that the people behind these games may eventually lose interest, moving on to whatever attention-grabbing scheme big tech facilitates next. The risk, of course, is that the audience also loses interest in what these storefronts offer before that happens. After all, nobody wants to wade through a tsunami of slop to get to the games they want to play.

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Rws7mDGqrkaXrNKCH4jZ2D-1920-80.png
I've played about 50+ hours of the World of Warcraft: Forever beta, and wouldn't you know it, I'm going to be playing a lot more when it comes out November 4.

Earlier this week, Kris Zierhut, principal game designer on World of Warcraft: Forever, said that the game would have a release schedule that's a "little more laid back" . Rather than the blisteringly fast eight to 10 week schedule of Season of Discovery, Forever'll aim to release major updates once every four months or so.

This is honestly music to my ears—I've been impressed by retail WoW's blistering pace and its seasonal structure, even if there have been some rocky, bug-filled patches in the past; and it's certainly something I've praised before, especially in contrast to other certain MMOs that have been coming to a standstill.

But I've been playing WoW… well, for a long time, but I've had a consistent sub since Dragonflight, and I've been able to see the arc of Blizzard whipping up its schedule into a proper roadmap . Which did pull the game back from the brink, true, but three expansions in and I'm just sort of exhausted.

There's always some new bar to fill, some new doohickey to collect, some new reputation track to chew on, and it all moves so fast that if I, say, have an off-week to go play another game, I feel pretty lost. While Midnight does major patches at roughly the same release tempo (12.0.0 came out in January, 12.1.0 came out in August) it also has a ton of interim stuff to flood out your schedule every three months, rather than four.

Launch was already crammed with stuff—a raid tier, delves, the new prey system, housing, and so on. Just under three months passed since launch, and wham, suddenly we've got Void Assaults! Ritual Sites! The Omnium Folio! Whatever Abyss Anglers is, I never checked, which is kinda the problem! Just over a month later, and there's a new raid and a new system plugged into Void Assaults (which I'm literally just now finding out about, I completely missed it). Two months later, and it's 12.1.0, which I hadn't even sat down to properly play before Labyrinths became a thing.

The idea of smaller, chiller patches in an overall slower-paced game (here's fellow PCG writer Lincoln Carpenter's treatise on the virtues of hitting a scorpion with a club for 38 seconds ) sounds like a nice, soothing bath after an overstimulating day at the circus.
I do feel that prickling sense of overstimulation fear return when Zierhut talks about the interim stuff, however:

"And then one nuance on that is: We do plan on making content that unlocks in between … you want to stagger out some content across those four months. It's not just patch day comes [around], here's a content fire hose, and now we're silent for four months. A lot of that is, hey, there's a time event calendar that gradually unlocks things and opens them up over those four months to give things a little bit more life instead of that all at once effect."

Still, given Forever's meant to be a horizontally-progressing game that doesn't have expansions ( we'll need to see how that pans out ), I might find these little tasks a lot more soothing than the looming feeling I have with WoW, where at any point it might suddenly become too late to get stuck into a season.

Ideally, these mid-patch trickles will be optional tasks I can get around to basically whenever, rather than something I feel pressured to get done just so I can stay up-to-date for whatever flashy system's trundling down the pipeline next. Hit me with that lo-fi update cadence, I'm ready for it.
